files.file: added MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS = 200 beside the other limits
_validate_description rejects trimmed len > 200 with 422 after the blank check; imports the constant
added 18 tests: POST/PUT length matrix (1, 200, 201, padded, emoji), rejected PUT unchanged, blank message unchanged, constant
maxlength=200 on the edit textarea; ERROR_HINTS entry for the new detail

tests.test: Full suite: 130 passed (112 existing + 18 new), including test_real_paths_untouched. No existing test needed updating.

commands_run.command: cd backend and run pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1)

design_decisions.decision: ERROR_HINTS uses substring match (includes) over an ordered list; new key "description must be at most 200 characters" overlaps no existing key, so inserted before "log not found" without shadowing.
Edit textarea uses setAttribute("maxlength","200") rather than the textarea.maxLength property, so the attribute is literally present as the criterion words it.
Detail string built from the constant via f-string; rejected hardcoding 200 in the message. The JS and HTML keep a literal 200 (no shared source).

implementation.self_critique: Frontend changes are not browser-tested here; the hint key must match the server string exactly (it does, lowercase compare). Browser maxlength counts UTF-16 units, so emoji hit the limit earlier than the server's code-point count (recorded, not reconciled).
